questions.q: What does setting a Trailhead profile to Public actually make visible to others?
options: Your certifications, community activity, badges, points, avatar, and about-me information
Nothing -- Public only affects search engine indexing
Your private login credentials
Only your name, with no other details
questions.explain: The lesson states a Public profile shows certifications, community activity, badges, points, avatar, and about-me information to anyone with the link.

questions.q: According to the real Trailhead rank ladder in this lesson, how many badges and points does the Ranger rank require?
options: 10 badges and 9,000 points
200 badges and 100,000+ points
1 badge and 200 points
100 badges and 50,000 points
questions.explain: The lesson's rank table lists Ranger at 100 badges and 50,000 points.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a high Trailblazer Rank alone isn't a strong hiring signal?
options: Because ranks are not visible on a public profile
Because only Superbadges count toward rank
Because rank is a volume signal, not a relevance signal -- it doesn't show the badges match the job
Because Salesforce removed the rank system entirely
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that rank measures volume, not relevance, and that a Hiker with the right trail can be a stronger candidate than a high-rank Trailblazer with unrelated badges.

questions.q: What makes a Superbadge a stronger signal than a typical badge, according to the lesson?
options: A Superbadge is a longer, hands-on, scenario-based challenge graded against a real Salesforce org, so it can't be passed by memorizing answers
A Superbadge is awarded automatically after enough regular badges
A Superbadge requires no Salesforce org at all
A Superbadge is only available to Architects
questions.explain: The lesson describes Superbadges as hands-on, scenario-based challenges that the platform grades against real work, making them harder to fake than a multiple-choice badge.

questions.q: What does the lesson say a Trail represents?
options: A single multiple-choice quiz
A guided, ordered sequence of badges built around a specific role or skill
A random, unordered list of any badges a user has completed
A private messaging feature within Trailhead
questions.explain: The lesson defines a Trail as a guided sequence of badges built around a specific role or skill, showing a reviewer you followed a structured curriculum.
